description: WATex is a Python machine-learning toolkit for groundwater exploration. Its maintainers document methods that combine electrical resistivity profiling, vertical sounding, short-period electromagnetic surveys, geology and hydrogeology to identify promising borehole sites and estimate well-water content. A user supplies local geophysical measurements and training labels; outputs are mapped candidate drilling sites, predicted flow or water-inrush values and diagnostic plots. Geography and measurement spacing follow the field survey; no fixed national water network or forecast period is bundled. The BSD-3-Clause source is free through GitHub, PyPI and conda-forge, with API examples including synthetic resistivity stations. A limitation is that the synthetic example demonstrates code behaviour, not groundwater yield in a real aquifer. Local geology, survey noise and independent borehole checks remain necessary before siting infrastructure. The toolkit supports drinking-water well planning and subsurface hazard screening. The catalogue's model-fao-aquacrop is a separate agricultural water model, not a direct dependency. No survey dataset or package was downloaded.
